plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 20, and bidders are rational, they won't bid their full value. Assuming others also follow this logic, a safe bid is a small increment above 0. However, my value is $36, significantly higher than the maximum possible value. Therefore, I can bid aggressively, aiming to win without overpaying. I will bid $1.00.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value of the highest of the remaining two bids is approximately 2/3 * 20 = $13.33. To win with certainty, I should bid slightly above this. However, since my value is $47, I can afford to bid higher. I will bid $13.40 to ensure I win.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and the auction mechanism (paying the second-highest bid), the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because any bid above your value risks winning and losing money, while a bid significantly below your value risks losing the auction to someone who values the item more. Since my value is $46, I will bid slightly below that.
